correctness.rationale: Any component-permuting algebra automorphism must preserve the neutral diagonal component because it contains the identity. It therefore permutes the primitive diagonal idempotents, say by \(\sigma\), and each one-dimensional matrix corner forces \(\varphi(E_{x,y})=d_xd_y^{-1}E_{\sigma(x),\sigma(y)}\), yielding the diagonal factor \(T_G=(k^\times)^G/k^\times\). If \(\pi\) is the induced degree permutation, the degree equation \(\sigma(x)^{-1}\sigma(y)=\pi(x^{-1}y)\) implies \(\pi(e)=e\), \(\sigma(y)=\sigma(e)\pi(y)\), and then \(\pi(xg)=\pi(x)\pi(g)\). Thus \(\pi\in\operatorname{Aut}(G)\) and \(\sigma\) is left-affine. Conversely every diagonal conjugation and left-affine permutation has the required action. Hence the full component-permuting group is \(T_G\rtimes\operatorname{Hol}(G)\), the componentwise stabilizer is \(T_G\rtimes G\), and the quotient is \(\operatorname{Aut}(G)\). The finite-field orders follow immediately. The package checker independently confirms the permutation factors for \(C_2,C_3,C_4,C_2^2,S_3\).
residual_risks: The theorem is for \(k\)-algebra automorphisms only and excludes semilinear field automorphisms.
